subject: MSA & Order Form: evidence timebox, escrow pre-approval, and redline note
messages:
From: Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@novalabs.com>
To: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaLabs Procurement <procurement@novalabs.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form — redlines + evidence timebox request

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and procurement at NovaLabs ran the MSA and Order Form by our internal review. We attached a set of redlines (high level) and have three points we need to resolve before procurement can greenlight the SOW: 

1) Indemnity carveouts: we want explicit language limiting customer cooperation to a single technical evidence submission (proof of origin / sample logs) and a timebox of 30 days post-notice for further evidence production.
2) Escrow / remediation funding: procurement requires a pre-approval checkbox for an escrow mechanism or insurance waterfall to be documented in the Order Form; they asked for examples.
3) Technical witness: for third-party IP claims we want the option to request a mutually agreed technical witness for evidence review; that needs a cadence and fee cap.

Please review the attached redline and tell us whether Redwood can accept a 30-day timebox, and whether you can provide a sample SOC2 and an example escrow clause or insurance certificate. Procurement would like an answer by next Friday (2024-03-22) to keep the timeline.

Attachments: NL-MSA-v2-redline.pdf

Best,
Sarah Meyer
Senior Counsel, NovaLabs
legal@novalabs.com


From: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@novalabs.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2024 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — redlines + evidence timebox request

Sarah — thanks for the clear list and the redlines. Quick thoughts inline below; I'll loop in legal ops (Lauren) and CS escalation (Ben) so we can confirm operational feasibility: 

- 30-day evidence timebox: operationally tight but reasonable for most infra/evidence requests; we need to preserve the right to request additional follow-up if new technical facts surface (propose language: "30 days for initial evidence; additional reasonable requests subject to mutual agreement and documented good-faith effort").
- Escrow / remediation funding: Redwood doesn't typically put money into escrow for customer-contracted usage, but we can sign an insurance waterfall clause and provide evidence of our commercial insurance. We can also accept a limited escrow provision for high-risk verticals with a one-time upfront fee to cover escrow admin.
- Technical witness: agree in principle; propose a mutually agreed pool and fee cap (e.g., up to $7,500) and a scheduling SLA (available within 21 business days).

Action items: Lauren — can you confirm whether Legal Ops can produce an insurance certificate sample and a short escrow template? Ben — can you confirm CS readiness for a 30-day turnaround for evidence collection and whether extra engineering support can be billed?

Markus Klein
Head of Business, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@novalabs.com>
To: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaLabs Procurement <procurement@novalabs.com>, legal@novalabs.com
Date: Sat, 16 Mar 2024 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — redlines + evidence timebox request

Hi Markus,

Appreciate the quick response and proposed compromises. Procurement confirmed that an insurance-waterfall + an optional escrow for certain customers would be acceptable. They asked for two concrete items from Redwood to include in the Order Form: 

A) Short escrow template (boilerplate clause) with an admin fee range.
B) An example certificate of insurance naming NovaLabs as an additional insured for indemnity purposes (or a carrier letter confirming coverage scope).

On the technical-side, procurement wants the technical witness fee cap to be explicit as a dollar cap in the Order Form (no ambiguous "fee cap" language). They also want the 30-day timebox to be a firm requirement — NovaLabs cannot accept open-ended follow-ups except for good cause (fraud, newly discovered code injection, etc.).

Also attached: an "evidence checklist" (spreadsheet) our SOC team uses to validate proof-of-origin for models/datasets. If Redwood can commit to delivering the initial evidence set in the checklist within the 30-day window, procurement will move the SOW to their signoff queue.

Attachments: evidence-checklist-template.xlsx

Best,
Sarah


From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@novalabs.com>, NovaLabs Procurement <procurement@novalabs.com>
Cc: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Mar 2024 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — redlines + evidence timebox request

Sarah / NovaLabs procurement team — looping back with proposed language and next steps. I've drafted a short set of redlines below that mirror your asks while preserving Redwood's operational constraints. If that looks good we can turn these into tracked changes in the Order Form and produce the certificate and escrow clause for signature: 

1) Evidence timebox (Order Form / MSA, Section X.X)
"""Customer shall provide notice of any third-party IP or infringement claim to Redwood. Redwood shall have an initial 30-calendar-day period to produce the technical evidence set listed in Appendix E (Initial Evidence). Customer may, for good cause, request additional discrete evidence beyond the Initial Evidence, limited to two supplemental requests, each not to exceed 14 calendar days. Any supplemental requests that materially expand scope require mutual written agreement."""

Rationale: commits to a clear 30-day initial window, allows strictly limited supplemental follow-ups for good cause — this meets procurement's need for predictability while giving us a path for necessary technical follow-up.

2) Escrow / Insurance (Order Form, Section Y.Y)
"""Redwood will provide a certificate of insurance evidencing commercial general liability and professional liability coverage; upon mutual written request for high-risk verticals, the Parties may agree to an escrow arrangement, for which Customer shall pay a one-time escrow administration fee not to exceed $5,000, and the escrow agent shall be mutually agreed."""

Rationale: we don't put operating cash into escrow by default. This language gives procurement the option and sets a clear admin fee cap.

3) Technical witness (Order Form, Section Z.Z)
"""If requested by Customer, the Parties will procure a mutually agreed technical expert to review evidence. The maximum out-of-pocket fee for such an expert shall be $7,500, plus reasonable travel expenses if in-person, to be paid by the requesting Party unless otherwise agreed."""

Rationale: explicit dollar cap and who pays removes ambiguity.

Next steps: 
- Sarah: confirm the three clauses above are acceptable in principle. If yes, I'll produce marked-up MSA/Order Form (tracked changes) and attach the sample COI and the escrow clause.
- Ben: please confirm CS/engineering can meet the 30-day initial evidence delivery for the checklist in the attachment. If there are any checklist items you can't produce within 30 days, note them now so we can flag exceptions.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if needed before final redlines.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
